Baseline Findings.Summary: Federal tax credit amount calculation contradicts qualified rehabilitation expenditures base in financial model
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 states qualified rehabilitation expenses are 24,600 ($ in thousands) and rate is 20%, but calculates federal credit as $5,120,000; DOC-06 states QRE of $24,600,000 generates $4,920,000 credit
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.2, 2.1-2.3: 'Qualified rehabilitation expenses: 24,600 ($ in thousands)' || DOC-05 p.2, 2.3: 'Federal historic tax credit: $5,120,000' || DOC-06 p.3, 4-5: 'Total qualified rehabilitation expenditures: $24,600,000' || DOC-06 p.3, 5: 'Federal rehabilitation credit: $4,920,000'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: At a 20% statutory credit rate under IRC Section 47, 20% of $24,600,000 is $4,920,000, not $5,120,000 (which would require $25,600,000 of QRE). DOC-05 internally miscalculates the credit amount or uses inconsistent figures. The CPA draft cost certification (DOC-06) governs over the model summary.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Virginia credit proceeds calculation contradicts state credit rate and formula in financial model
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 states QRE of 24,600 ($ in thousands), Virginia credit rate of 25%, and price of 0.85 per credit dollar, but states proceeds of 5,227.5 ($ in thousands); DOC-12/13 states expected credits of $6,150,000
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.2, 2.1: 'Qualified rehabilitation expenses: 24,600 ($ in thousands)' || DOC-05 p.2, 2.6-2.8: 'Virginia credit price per credit dollar: 0.85' || DOC-05 p.2, 2.7: 'Virginia credit proceeds: 5,227.5 ($ in thousands)' || DOC-05 p.2, 2.8: 'Virginia historic tax credit rate: 25%' || DOC-12 p.2, 1.1: 'Credits means the Virginia historic rehabilitation tax credits allocated to Seller for the Project, expected to total $6,150,000.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Under Virginia law, a 25% credit on $24,600,000 yields $6,150,000 in state credits. At $0.85 per credit dollar, the proceeds should equal $5,227,500 ($5,227.5 thousand); however, DOC-04 Sources and Uses lists Virginia credit proceeds as $5,043,000 ($6,150,000 at $0.82, matching the older signed contract rate). The financial model and development budget are contradictory.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Same underlying issue as F03 (model uses the draft price). Summary says the model's math is wrong, but the explanation shows it is right; the real conflict is the price.

We have updated the model to reflect it.' || DOC-16 p.1, 3: 'Virginia credits sold at $0.85 per credit.'

Baseline Findings.Summary: Contradiction on tax year for claiming federal historic tax credits
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 states federal credits are delivered in tax year 2025; DOC-16 states credits will be claimed on the 2024 return; DOC-06 and DOC-09 establish placed-in-service date in 2025
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.4, 4.1: 'Federal credits delivered: 2025 5,120; 2026 to 2029 0 ($ in thousands)' || DOC-16 p.2, 5: 'Federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return.' || DOC-06 p.1, 2: 'The building was placed in service on July 15, 2025' || DOC-09 p.2, 14: '7/15/2025 Placed in service'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Under Treas. Reg. Section 1.48-12(f)(2) and IRC Section 47, rehabilitation tax credits can only be claimed in the taxable year the property is placed in service. Because the building was placed in service in 2025, claiming credits on the 2024 tax return as stated in DOC-16 is legally impossible and constitutes a major compliance issue.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Right conclusion, but cites the pre-2018 rule. Credits are claimed over five years from 2025. It cited the model's all-in-2025 line without flagging it (HTC01-035 missed).

Baseline Findings.Summary: Contradiction regarding placed-in-service date of the property
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-06, DOC-09, DOC-11 recital state placed in service is July 15, 2025; DOC-15 states building was placed in service on March 28 with Phase 1 TCO
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-06 p.1, 2: 'The building was placed in service on July 15, 2025, being the date the completed rehabilitation was ready and available for its intended use.' || DOC-09 p.2, 14: '7/15/2025 Placed in service' || DOC-11 p.14, 4.2(b): '[Recital added by First Amendment:] the Building was placed in service on July 15, 2025.' || DOC-15 p.8: 'Building placed in service March 28 with the Phase 1 TCO. Residents have started moving in on floors 1 to 3.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The placed-in-service date determines the tax credit year, the measuring period for the substantial rehabilitation test under IRC Section 47(c)(1)(C), and the start of the 5-year recapture period. An early partial placed-in-service date in March 2025 contradicts the CPA's July 15, 2025 certification date and schedule milestones.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Severity overstated: both dates fall in 2025, so the credit year does not change. Expected Medium.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Ineligible non-depreciable site and FF&E costs classified as qualified expenses in development budget
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 classifies parking lot ($420,000) and furniture, fixtures and equipment ($290,000) as qualified costs; DOC-06 excludes parking, site work outside the building, and furniture from QRE

Baseline Findings.Explanation: Under IRC Section 47(c)(2)(B) and Treas. Reg. Section 1.48-12(c)(5), expenditures for parking lots, site improvements outside the building, and personal property (FF&E) do not qualify as Qualified Rehabilitation Expenditures (QRE). DOC-04 improperly includes $710,000 of unqualified expenses in its QRE total of $25,310,000. DOC-06 governs.

Section 8.2 No sale or transfer of the Building or any unit during the Compliance Period without Investor Member consent, including any conversion of the Building or any part of it to condominium ownership.'

Baseline Findings.Summary: Internal arithmetic error in capital contribution installment percentages in operating agreement

Baseline Findings.Explanation: The August 1, 2025 budget is $250,000 over the cap. The first amendment of that date, as excerpted, adds only the placed-in-service recital and does not raise the cap. The signed operating agreement governs, and consent is not shown.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Sources are $600,000 short of uses, but the investor memo says the project is fully funded.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 shows total sources of $31,150,000, total uses of $31,750,000, and a $600,000 gap; DOC-16 says the project is fully funded with all sources committed.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-04 p.1, line 12: 'Total sources' '$31,150,000' || DOC-04 p.1, line 24: 'Total uses $31,750,000' '$31,750,000' || DOC-04 p.1, line 25: 'Gap ($600,000)' '($600,000)' || DOC-04 p.1, line 7: 'Deferred developer fee' '$600,000' || DOC-16 p.1, 2: 'The project is fully funded, with all sources committed and construction complete.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The line items add to the printed source and use totals. The $600,000 deferred fee is already inside the $31,150,000 sources, so it does not close the gap. The budget is the source document and governs the memo.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The stated equity installments do not add up to the investor's $4,329,600 contribution.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-11 sets the contribution at $4,329,600 and labels the third installment as 40%, but that installment is stated as $1,831,840 rather than 40% of the total.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-11 p.13, 4.1: 'The Investor Member shall contribute a total of $4,329,600' || DOC-11 p.14, 4.2(a): '$865,920, being 20% of the capital contribution' || DOC-11 p.14, 4.2(b): '$1,298,880, being 30% of the capital contribution' || DOC-11 p.14, 4.2(c): '$1,831,840, being 40% upon receipt of Part 3 approval' || DOC-11 p.14, 4.2(d): '$432,960, being 10% of the capital contribution'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The 20%, 30%, and 10% amounts match $4,329,600. Forty percent is $1,731,840, not $1,831,840. The four stated installments add to $4,429,600, which is $100,000 more than the contribution the same article fixes. The operating agreement contradicts itself.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The budget's hard-cost line items add to $22,140,000, not the $22,540,000 subtotal used as qualified cost.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 states a hard-cost subtotal of $22,540,000 and marks it qualified; the line items on that page add to $22,140,000.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-04 p.2, line 22: 'Hard cost subtotal $22,540,000' 'Yes' '$22,540,000' || DOC-04 p.2, line 38: 'Total qualified costs $25,310,000' '$25,310,000'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Lines 3 through 21, from general conditions through bonds and permits, add to $22,140,000, which is $400,000 below the printed subtotal. The qualified total of $25,310,000 uses the higher subtotal, so that total is not supported by its own lines. The signed adjusted contract sum is $22,540,000, but this schedule does not build to it.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: First model to catch this one.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The operating agreement caps the recapture guaranty at $1,500,000 in the body and at $1,000,000 in the guaranty form.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-11 Article 7 caps recapture indemnity at $1,500,000; Exhibit C of the same agreement caps it at $1,000,000.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-11 p.21, 7.4: 'The Guarantor shall indemnify the Investor Member for any recapture of federal credits caused by an act or omission of the Managing Member, up to a maximum of $1,500,000.' || DOC-11 p.42, 2: 'The total liability of the Guarantor for recapture under this Guaranty shall not exceed $1,000,000.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Both caps are in the same amended operating agreement, and the visible amendment does not reconcile them. The investor's recapture protection is uncertain by $500,000, and either cap is far below the roughly $4,920,000 federal credit.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The model collects Virginia credit proceeds on July 31, 2026, after the buyer's April 30, 2026 walk date and outside a 30-day closing.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 says Virginia proceeds are received July 31, 2026; DOC-12 lets the buyer terminate if certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026 and requires closing within 30 days after delivery.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.4, 4.4: 'Virginia credit proceeds received July 31, 2026' || DOC-12 p.6, 5.3: 'If the DHR certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026, Buyer may terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of the deposit.' || DOC-12 p.5, 5.1: 'Closing shall take place within thirty days after Seller delivers the DHR Certification to Buyer.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Payment on July 31, 2026 would require a certification delivered around July 1, 2026, which is after the buyer can already terminate. If certification is delivered by April 30, 2026, closing is due by about May 30, 2026, not July 31. The signed purchase agreement governs the model forecast.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The memo says Virginia has issued final credit certification, but no certification is in the data room.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-16 says Virginia DHR has issued final certification; the data room has no DHR certificate.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-16 p.2, 6: 'Virginia DHR has issued final certification for the state credits.' || DOC-12 p.2, 1.2: 'DHR Certification means the final certification of the Credits issued by the Virginia Department of Historic Resources.' || DOC-09 p.2: 'Part 3 submitted' '9/30/2025'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: State-credit proceeds and closing depend on that certificate. The only support is the October 1, 2025 memo, one day after the Part 3 submission date on the schedule. The certificate cannot be verified, so the memo does not govern.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The investor memo treats the cost certification as established, but the only CPA report is a draft marked not for reliance.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-16 says the cost certification shows about $24.6 million of qualified expenses and was prepared by an independent CPA; DOC-06 is a September 15, 2025 draft and says it is not for reliance.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-06 p.1: 'DRAFT - FOR DISCUSSION PURPOSES ONLY - NOT FOR RELIANCE' || DOC-06 p.1: 'Draft dated September 15, 2025' || DOC-05 p.1, 1.3: 'The model will be updated when the cost certification is final.' || DOC-16 p.1, 4: 'The cost certification shows approximately $24.6 million of qualified rehabilitation expenditures, generating $4.9M in federal credits.' || DOC-16 p.2, 3: 'The cost certification has been prepared by an independent CPA.' || DOC-04 p.3, 2: 'Final qualified rehabilitation expenses will be set by the cost certification.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: A draft that disclaims reliance is not a final certification of the credit base. The memo uses those figures as if they were final. No final cost certification is in the data room.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Valid issue not in the ground truth: the memo presents a draft, not-for-reliance cost certification as final. Candidate new case.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The equity bridge that is to be repaid from federal installment 3 matures before the only date given for that installment.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 says the $1,700,000 bridge matures on March 31, 2026 and is repaid from federal equity installment 3; DOC-05 says installment 3 is received on June 30, 2026.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-04 p.1, line 9: 'Equity bridge loan $1,700,000, matures 3/31/2026' || DOC-04 p.1, line 10: 'Interim only; repaid from federal equity installment 3' || DOC-05 p.4, 4.3: 'Installment 3 received June 30, 2026' || DOC-11 p.14, 4.2(c): '$1,831,840, being 40% upon receipt of Part 3 approval from the National Park Service.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The repayment source in the model arrives three months after the loan matures. The operating agreement triggers installment 3 on Part 3 approval rather than on a calendar date, and that approval is not documented. The March 1, 2025 model is an earlier forecast, but it is the only dated receipt and it does not support repayment by maturity.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Severity understated: expected High.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The appraisal describes 86 rental units plus commercial space, while the other project documents describe 84 apartments and 2 commercial suites.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-10 says 86 units of rental housing with commercial space on the ground floor; DOC-03 and DOC-07 say 84 apartments and 2 commercial suites.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-10 p.2, 1: 'Proposed improvements: 86 units of rental housing in a converted five-story mill, with commercial space on the ground floor.' || DOC-03 p.1, 2: 'The subject will contain 84 apartments and 2 commercial suites.' || DOC-07 p.1, 1: 'The project converts the former Ashby Mill into 84 apartments and 2 ground-floor commercial suites'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Eighty-four apartments plus two commercial suites is not 86 rental units plus commercial space. The appraisal was the bank's underwriting basis. The later architectural scope and the market study agree with each other and are the better description of the project that was built.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The financial model leases up at 12 units a month, and the market study it relies on uses 7.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 assumes 12 units per month; DOC-03 projects 7 units per month to a 93% stabilization.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.3, 3.1: 'Average monthly rent per unit is based on the market study, increased by three percent a year.' || DOC-05 p.3, 3.2: 'Lease-up assumption: 12 units per month from the first unit delivered.' || DOC-03 p.8, 4: 'We project an absorption pace of 7 units per month; stabilization in about 12 months, defined as 93% physical occupancy.' || DOC-09 p.2: 'Stabilization (93% occupancy)' '9/30/2026'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: At 84 apartments, 93% occupancy is about 78 units. Twelve units a month is roughly six and a half months, which does not land on the September 30, 2026 stabilization date; seven units a month is about eleven months. The study and the model cannot both be the lease-up pace.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The June 5, 2023 construction contract incorporates later documents, including a Part 2 approval that did not yet exist, and starts work before the schedule does.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-08 is dated June 5, 2023, tells the contractor to begin on the notice-to-proceed date, and includes July 20, 2023 drawings and an approved Part 2; DOC-02 approves Part 2 on August 22, 2023; DOC-09 starts construction on October 2, 2023.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: On June 5, 2023 the specifications were not yet issued and Part 2 was not approved, so the contract cannot already include them. The schedule, which marks the October 2, 2023 start as actual, conflicts with a notice to proceed that starts work on June 5. The approval letter and the schedule govern the dates.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Severity understated: expected High. Also covers the new candidate case (contract dated before the documents it cites).

Baseline Findings.Summary: The completion and recapture guarantor is never named.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-11 imposes guaranty obligations on 'the Guarantor' but does not identify that party.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-11 p.21, 7.1: 'The Guarantor shall guarantee completion of the rehabilitation in accordance with the plans and specifications.' || DOC-11 p.42, 1: 'The Guarantor unconditionally guarantees to the Investor Member the obligations of the Managing Member described in Article 7 of the Operating Agreement.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Completion and recapture protection depend on a named, creditworthy guarantor. No guaranty signature block or guarantor name appears in the operating agreement or Exhibit C. The obligation cannot be verified.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: True of the excerpt, but DOC-11 is marked as an excerpt, so the definition may sit in pages not provided. Decide whether it becomes a Low or Medium case.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The appraisal's value conclusions cannot be read, so the construction-loan value is unsupported.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-10 says it contains the value conclusions and that as-is value is used for loan-to-value; the value figures on page 4 are obscured, and page 5 points to a full report that is not in the data room.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-10 p.1, 1: 'Purpose: to estimate the as-is market value of the fee simple interest and the prospective value upon completion of the proposed rehabilitation.' || DOC-10 p.1, 4: 'This excerpt contains the property description and the value conclusions only.' || DOC-10 p.4, 3: 'The as-is value is used by the lender as the starting point for the loan-to-value calculation.' || DOC-10 p.5, 1: 'The prospective value upon completion and stabilization is set out in the full report.' || DOC-04 p.1, line 3: 'Construction loan - Piedmont Community Bank' '$18,500,000'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Page 4's value conclusion is covered and paragraph 1 is not readable. No as-is or prospective value figure can be verified against the $18,500,000 loan. The missing full report is not a substitute.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Flags the unreadable page but links it to the loan, not to the adjusted basis in DOC-06.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The budget counts the parking lot and furniture as qualified rehabilitation costs, and the draft cost certification excludes them.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 marks the $420,000 parking lot and $290,000 furniture as qualified; DOC-06 excludes parking, site work outside the building, and furniture.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-04 p.2, line 31: 'Parking lot' 'Yes' '$420,000' || DOC-04 p.2, line 34: 'Furniture, fixtures and equipment' 'Yes' '$290,000' || DOC-04 p.2, line 38: 'Total qualified costs $25,310,000' || DOC-04 p.3, 2: 'Qualified costs are an estimate prepared by the developer. Final qualified rehabilitation expenses will be set by the cost certification.' || DOC-06 p.3, 1: 'Costs for acquisition, land, site work outside the building, parking and furniture are excluded.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Both can be true at different stages: the budget says its qualified total is an estimate, and the later draft certification removes items that are generally not qualified rehabilitation expenditures under Treas. Reg. section 1.48-12. The $710,000 difference is worth confirming because the budget total has not been revised and the certification is not final.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Wrong class and severity: parking and furniture never qualify, so this is a Critical contradiction, not an estimate difference. It counts as a false alarm on class.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The architectural specifications spell the owner as Ashbey Mill Owner LLC.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-07 names the owner Ashbey Mill Owner LLC; DOC-01, DOC-08, and DOC-11 name Ashby Mill Owner LLC.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-07 p.1: 'OWNER: Ashbey Mill Owner LLC' || DOC-01 p.1, 1: 'Owner of record: Ashby Mill Owner LLC' || DOC-08 p.1: 'Ashby Mill Owner LLC (Owner)' || DOC-11 p.1: 'Ashby Mill Owner LLC, a Virginia limited liability company (the Company)'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Ashbey and Ashby are different spellings, not an LLC versus L.L.C. variant. The owner documents agree on Ashby. The specification header looks like a typo and does not by itself change who owns the building, but it should be corrected before it is used as a contract document.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Federal historic tax credit amount and basis calculation conflict across documents.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 states federal historic tax credit is $5,120,000 on QRE of $24,600,000; DOC-06 states federal rehabilitation credit is $4,920,000 on QRE of $24,600,000.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.2, 2.1-2.3: 'Qualified rehabilitation expenses: 24,600 ($ in thousands)' and 'Federal historic tax credit rate: 20%' and 'Federal historic tax credit: $5,120,000' || DOC-06 p.3, 4-5: 'Total qualified rehabilitation expenditures: $24,600,000' and 'Federal rehabilitation credit: $4,920,000' || DOC-11 p.13, 4.1(a): 'projected federal credits of $4,920,000'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: At a 20% federal credit rate, 20% of $24,600,000 is $4,920,000, not $5,120,000. DOC-05 miscalculates the credit (which would require $25,600,000 of QRE), whereas the CPA cost certification and operating agreement govern with $4,920,000.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Total qualified costs in development budget include ineligible non-depreciable site work and personal property.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 classifies parking lot ($420,000) and furniture, fixtures and equipment ($290,000) as qualified costs; DOC-06 states costs for site work outside the building, parking, and furniture are excluded.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-04 p.2, 31, 34, 38: 'Parking lot | Yes | $420,000' and 'Furniture, fixtures and equipment | Yes | $290,000' and 'Total qualified costs $25,310,000 | $25,310,000' || DOC-06 p.3, 1: 'Costs for acquisition, land, site work outside the building, parking and furniture are excluded.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Under IRC Section 47 and Treas. Reg. 1.48-12, qualified rehabilitation expenditures (QRE) must be chargeable to the capital account of the certified historic structure; site improvements/parking lots and personal property (FF&E) do not qualify. DOC-06 CPA cost certification correctly excludes them, reducing QRE.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Window replacement specifications and quotation violate NPS Part 2 condition of approval and architect specifications.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-02 and DOC-07 require replacement windows to replicate original wood profiles and muntin pattern; DOC-14 quotes white vinyl replacement windows with simulated grilles between glass and aluminum panning.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-02 p.3, Condition 2: 'Replacement windows must replicate the original wood profiles in material, dimensions and muntin pattern.' || DOC-07 p.6, 1: 'Wood windows replicating original profiles, with true divided lites matching the historic muntin pattern and profile.' || DOC-14 p.1, Item 1-2: 'Vinyl double-hung, standard profile' and 'Aluminum panning at masonry openings' and 'Units are white vinyl with a standard sash profile and simulated grilles between the glass.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Installing vinyl windows with between-the-glass grilles instead of wood windows matching original historic profiles directly breaches NPS Part 2 Condition 2, jeopardizing Part 3 certification and the entire federal and state historic tax credits.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Did not raise the missing NPS approval of shop drawings (HTC01-010 missed).

Baseline Findings.Summary: Planned commercial unit sale violates operating agreement 5-year compliance period restrictions and creates federal credit recapture risk.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-15 states a plan to sell commercial unit C-1 to Danville Arts Collective in June 2026; DOC-11 strictly forbids sale or transfer of the building or any unit during the 5-year compliance period.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-15 p.12, Update, Oct 2025: 'We plan to sell commercial unit C-1 to Danville Arts Collective, targeting June 30, 2026.' || DOC-11 p.24, Section 8.1-8.2: 'Compliance Period: five years beginning on the placed-in-service date of the Building.' and 'No sale or transfer of the Building or any unit during the Compliance Period without Investor Member consent, including any conversion of the Building or any part of it to condominium ownership.' || DOC-16 p.2, 7: 'No sale or transfer of any part of the property is planned during the credit period.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Under IRC Section 50(a), a disposition of a portion of the building during the 5-year compliance period triggers tax credit recapture. The developer update reveals an active plan to sell unit C-1 in 2026, directly contradicting the Investor Memo and breaching Section 8.2 of the Operating Agreement.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Tax year for claiming federal historic tax credits contradicts placed-in-service year.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-16 states federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 tax return; DOC-05, DOC-06, DOC-09, and DOC-11 establish placed in service occurred in 2025.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-16 p.2, 5: 'Federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return.' || DOC-06 p.1, 2: 'The building was placed in service on July 15, 2025, being the date the completed rehabilitation was ready and available for its intended use.' || DOC-05 p.4, 4.1: 'Federal credits delivered: 2025 5,120; 2026 to 2029 0' || DOC-09 p.2, 14: 'Placed in service | 7/15/2025' || DOC-11 p.14, Section 4.2(b): 'the Building was placed in service on July 15, 2025.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Under Treasury regulations for the historic rehabilitation credit, credits cannot be claimed in a tax year prior to the taxable year in which the qualified rehabilitated building is placed in service (2025). Claiming credits on the 2024 tax return is invalid.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Cited the model's all-in-2025 line as support without flagging it (HTC01-035 missed).

Baseline Findings.Summary: Governing Virginia tax credit purchase price is $0.82 per signed agreement, whereas model, memo, and email cite $0.85 based on an unexecuted draft.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-12 signed agreement sets the purchase price at $0.82 per credit dollar; DOC-05, DOC-13, DOC-15, and DOC-16 assert a price of $0.85 per credit dollar.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-12 p.3, Section 2.1: 'Price. Buyer shall pay $0.82 per $1.00 of credit for all Credits transferred at Closing.' || DOC-05 p.2, 2.6: 'Virginia credit price per credit dollar: 0.85' || DOC-13 p.3, Section 2.1: 'Price. Buyer shall pay $0.85 per $1.00 of credit for all Credits transferred at Closing.' || DOC-15 p.6, Email, Mar 4, 2025: 'pricing came in at 85 cents. We have updated the model to reflect it.' || DOC-16 p.1, 3: 'Virginia credits sold at $0.85 per credit.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: DOC-12 is the fully signed agreement dated November 4, 2024. DOC-13 is explicitly marked 'Draft dated February 18, 2025 - not for execution', so the signed contract ($0.82) legally governs over unexecuted drafts and email assertions, representing an overstatement of state credit proceeds.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Total developer fee in development budget exceeds the contractual cap in the Operating Agreement.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 allocates a total developer fee of $2,750,000; DOC-11 caps the total development fee at $2,500,000 without prior written consent.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-04 p.1, Uses 22: 'Developer fee $2,750,000' || DOC-11 p.18, Section 6.3: 'The total development fee shall not exceed $2,500,000 without the prior written consent of the Investor Member.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The budget's $2,750,000 developer fee exceeds the $2,500,000 cap by $250,000. There is no documentation in the data room showing Investor Member written consent to exceed the contractual cap.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Conflict between Operating Agreement Article 7 and Exhibit C on Guarantor recapture liability cap.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-11 Section 7.4 states the Guarantor recapture indemnification is up to a maximum of $1,500,000; DOC-11 Exhibit C states total liability of the Guarantor for recapture shall not exceed $1,000,000.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-11 p.21, Section 7.4: 'The Guarantor shall indemnify the Investor Member for any recapture of federal credits caused by an act or omission of the Managing Member, up to a maximum of $1,500,000.' || DOC-11 p.42, Exhibit C 2: 'The total liability of the Guarantor for recapture under this Guaranty shall not exceed $1,000,000.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The body of the Operating Agreement provides a $1.5M recapture guaranty cap, but the attached form of guaranty in Exhibit C limits liability to $1.0M, creating an internal legal inconsistency regarding investor protection.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Construction contract sum does not match between GC Agreement Exhibit D and Draft Cost Certification.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-08 Exhibit D establishes an adjusted contract sum after approved change orders of $22,540,000; DOC-06 draft cost certification lists the construction contract at $21,900,000.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-08 p.9, Exhibit D: 'Adjusted contract sum after change orders $22,540,000' || DOC-06 p.2, 3: 'Construction contract $21,900,000'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: DOC-08 demonstrates three signed change orders totaling $640,000 added to the original $21,900,000 base contract. DOC-06 uses the unadjusted original contract sum of $21,900,000 rather than the final adjusted contract sum.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Virginia state credit closing date in Financial Model is after the contractual outside termination date.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 assumes receipt of Virginia credit proceeds on July 31, 2026; DOC-12 provides that Buyer may terminate if DHR certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.4, 4.4: 'Virginia credit proceeds received July 31, 2026' || DOC-12 p.6, Section 5.3: 'If the DHR certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026, Buyer may terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of the deposit.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Under DOC-12 Section 5.1, closing must occur within 30 days after delivering DHR certification. Funding on July 31, 2026 indicates DHR certification occurs well after the April 30, 2026 outside termination date, putting buyer closing and proceeds at risk.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Discrepancy in project residential unit count between appraisal and all other documents.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-10 states the proposed improvements consist of 86 units of rental housing; DOC-03, DOC-07, and DOC-15 specify 84 apartment units.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-10 p.2, 1: 'Proposed improvements: 86 units of rental housing in a converted five-story mill, with commercial space on the ground floor.' || DOC-03 p.1, 2: 'The subject will contain 84 apartments and 2 commercial suites.' || DOC-07 p.1, 1: 'The project converts the former Ashby Mill into 84 apartments and 2 ground-floor commercial suites' || DOC-15 p.9, Update, Apr 2025: '48 units complete and leasing'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The appraisal evaluated 86 residential units, whereas architectural specifications, market study, and developer reports reflect 84 units, creating an inconsistency in underwriting density and unit configuration.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Cites DOC-15's 48 units as if it supported 84; it is a progress figure.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Projected absorption pace in financial model contradicts the market feasibility study.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 projects a lease-up absorption pace of 12 units per month; DOC-03 explicitly projects 7 units per month and cautions that a faster pace would require price discounting.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.3, 3.2: 'Lease-up assumption: 12 units per month from the first unit delivered.' || DOC-03 p.8, 4-5: 'We project an absorption pace of 7 units per month; stabilization in about 12 months, defined as 93% physical occupancy. A faster pace would require pricing below the proposed rents and is not assumed.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The financial model relies on an aggressive 12 units/month pace that the third-party market study explicitly rejected without rent reductions, artificially accelerating projected cash flow and stabilization.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Contract execution date in GC Agreement precedes date of contract documents incorporated by reference.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-08 states the agreement was entered into as of June 5, 2023, but incorporates architect drawings and specifications dated July 20, 2023 and the Part 2 approval.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-08 p.1, 3-4: 'The Contract Documents include the drawings and specifications issued by Hollins and Reade Architects dated July 20, 2023, and the approved Part 2 application. This Agreement is entered into as of June 5, 2023.' || DOC-02 p.1: 'August 22, 2023' || DOC-07 p.1: 'ISSUE: JULY 20, 2023'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: A contract executed on June 5, 2023 references specifications dated July 20, 2023 and an NPS approval not granted until August 22, 2023, indicating backdating or drafting errors in contract execution.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Same new candidate case found by every run so far: the contract is dated before the documents it cites.

Baseline Findings.Summary: NPS Part 3 certification approval claimed by developer lacks official documentation in the data room.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-15 states that NPS approved Part 3 in October 2025; no NPS Part 3 approval form or official certification is present in the data room.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-15 p.11, Email, Nov 3, 2025: 'Quick note: NPS approved Part 3 in October. We will send the paperwork once we have it in hand and request the third installment.' || DOC-09 p.2, 16: 'Part 3 submitted | 9/30/2025'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Under DOC-11 Section 4.2(c), installment 3 ($1,831,840) requires receipt of official Part 3 approval from the NPS. Informal email assertion without the certified Part 3 document leaves credit eligibility and funding condition unverified.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Quoted $1,831,840 for installment 3 without noticing it should be $1,731,840 (HTC01-014 missed).

Baseline Findings.Summary: Virginia DHR final certification of state tax credits claimed in Investor Memo is missing from the data room.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-16 claims Virginia DHR has issued final certification for the state credits; no DHR certification letter or state approval is included in the data room.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-16 p.2, 6: 'Virginia DHR has issued final certification for the state credits.' || DOC-12 p.2, Section 1.2: 'DHR Certification means the final certification of the Credits issued by the Virginia Department of Historic Resources.'

Baseline Findings.Summary: The draft cost certification names the developer rather than the property owner as the taxpayer.

Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-15 says the developer plans to sell commercial unit C-1 by June 30, 2026; DOC-16 says no sale or transfer of any part of the property is planned; DOC-11 prohibits transfers without consent.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-15 p.12, Update Oct 2025: 'We plan to sell commercial unit C-1 to Danville Arts Collective, targeting June 30, 2026.' || DOC-16 p.2, 7: 'No sale or transfer of any part of the property is planned during the credit period.' || DOC-11 p.24, Section 8.2: 'No sale or transfer of the Building or any unit during the Compliance Period without Investor Member consent, including any conversion of the Building or any part of it to condominium ownership.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Selling unit C-1 during the 5-year compliance period (July 2025 to July 2030) triggers partial credit recapture under IRC Section 50(a) and directly breaches DOC-11 Section 8.2 transfer restrictions. DOC-11 governs.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The developer claims Part 3 certification was approved by NPS, but no approval documentation is in the data room.

We will send the paperwork once we have it in hand and request the third installment.' || DOC-11 p.14, Section 4.2(c): '$1,831,840, being 40% upon receipt of Part 3 approval from the National Park Service.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The email acknowledges that paperwork is not in hand, and no NPS certification is provided. Investor funding of the 40% equity installment is legally contingent upon Part 3 approval.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The equity bridge loan matures three months before the third equity installment scheduled to repay it is received.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 says the equity bridge loan matures on March 31, 2026 and is repaid from installment 3; DOC-05 projects installment 3 will be received on June 30, 2026.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: Installment 3 is projected for receipt on June 30, 2026, leaving a three-month liquidity gap after the bridge loan matures on March 31, 2026, which creates maturity default exposure.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The appraisal report states the project consists of 86 units, whereas architectural specifications and market study state 84 units.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-10 says proposed improvements include 86 units of rental housing; DOC-03 and DOC-07 state the project contains 84 apartments.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-10 p.2, 1: 'Proposed improvements: 86 units of rental housing in a converted five-story mill, with commercial space on the ground floor.' || DOC-03 p.1, 2: 'The subject will contain 84 apartments and 2 commercial suites.' || DOC-07 p.1, 1: 'The project converts the former Ashby Mill into 84 apartments and 2 ground-floor commercial suites'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: A two-unit discrepancy alters gross rentable area, rent roll underwriting, and density. The architect's construction drawings and scope (DOC-07) govern physical building specifications over the bank appraisal excerpt.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The financial model lease-up velocity assumption exceeds the absorption rate established in the market study.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-03 projects an absorption pace of 7 units per month and notes a faster pace is not assumed; DOC-05 assumes a lease-up pace of 12 units per month.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: The financial model assumes lease-up at 12 units per month (over 70% faster than the market study's 7 units per month), which the market study explicitly warns would require rental price concessions. DOC-03 governs market demand underwriting.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The as-is building valuation in the appraisal report excerpt is obscured and unreadable.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-10 contains an illegible blurred line where the building as-is market value should be; DOC-04 and DOC-06 claim building acquisition basis of $1,540,000.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-10 p.4, 1: 'Value of the building' [blurred/illegible text] || DOC-04 p.1, 14: 'Acquisition - building $1,540,000' || DOC-06 p.4, 7: 'Adjusted basis $1,540,000'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The as-is appraised value of the building cannot be read from the document, preventing verification of the purchase price and starting adjusted basis utilized for the substantial rehabilitation test.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Full catch: ties the unreadable page to the adjusted basis used in the substantial rehabilitation test.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The investor summary memo claims the project is fully funded with all sources committed despite a $600,000 budget gap.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-16 claims the project is fully funded with all sources committed; DOC-04 shows an unfunded financing gap of ($600,000) between sources and uses.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-16 p.1, 2: 'The project is fully funded, with all sources committed and construction complete.' || DOC-04 p.1, 12, 24, 25: 'Total sources $31,150,000' and 'Total uses $31,750,000 $31,750,000' and 'Gap ($600,000) ($600,000)'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Total uses ($31,750,000) exceed total sources ($31,150,000) by $600,000, leaving an unfunded development deficit that contradicts the assertion in DOC-16 that all funding sources are committed. The detailed development budget (DOC-04) governs.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The architect scope and specifications header misspells the property owning entity name.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-07 identifies the owner as Ashbey Mill Owner LLC; DOC-01 and DOC-11 identify the owner as Ashby Mill Owner LLC.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-07 p.1, header: 'PROJECT: ASHBY MILL LOFTS | OWNER: Ashbey Mill Owner LLC' || DOC-01 p.1, 1: 'Owner of record: Ashby Mill Owner LLC, a Virginia limited liability company' || DOC-11 p.1, Preamble: 'Operating Agreement of Ashby Mill Owner LLC, a Virginia limited liability company'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The owner name is misspelled as 'Ashbey' rather than 'Ashby' in the specifications header. The formal formation and organizational documents (DOC-01, DOC-11) govern.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Cost certification names Riverside Heritage Development LLC as taxpayer while the owner and operating company is Ashby Mill Owner LLC.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-06 says taxpayer is Riverside Heritage Development LLC; DOC-01 says owner of record is Ashby Mill Owner LLC; DOC-11 says the Company owns the Building.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: The HTC claimant must be the owner or tax owner; a cost certification in a different taxpayer's name is a critical party mismatch. Signed ownership and operating documents govern over the draft cost certification.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Approved Part 2 requires wood replacement windows matching original profiles, but the window quotation is for vinyl units with simulated grilles.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-02 requires wood profiles and true historic muntin pattern; DOC-14 quotes vinyl double-hung units with simulated grilles between the glass.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: Vinyl windows with simulated grilles do not meet the approved Condition 2 material and muntin requirements and could jeopardize Part 3 certification. The approved Part 2 application governs.

Baseline Findings.Summary: No evidence shows NPS approved the window shop drawings before installation; the update only says drawings were sent to SHPO for NPS review.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-02 requires NPS approval before installation; DOC-15 says drawings were sent for review; DOC-09 shows windows installed later.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-02 p.3, Condition 2: 'Shop drawings for replacement windows must be submitted to and approved by NPS before installation.' || DOC-15 p.2, Mar 2024: 'Window shop drawings were sent to the SHPO for NPS review in February.' || DOC-09 p.1, 8: 'Windows floors 1 to 3 9/20/2024'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Sending shop drawings for review is not evidence of NPS approval, and no approval letter is in the data room. This is an unverified approval condition.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Severity overstated: expected High.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Placed-in-service date is March 28 in a developer update but July 15 in the cost certification and construction schedule.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-15 says the building was placed in service March 28 with the Phase 1 TCO; DOC-06 and DOC-09 say July 15, 2025.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-15 p.8: 'Building placed in service March 28 with the Phase 1 TCO.' || DOC-06 p.1, 2: 'The building was placed in service on July 15, 2025' || DOC-09 p.2, 14: 'Placed in service 7/15/2025'

Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Severity overstated: both dates fall in 2025, so the credit year does not change. Expected Medium. Calls the draft cost certification final.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Investor memo says federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return, but the building was placed in service July 15, 2025.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-16 says 2024 return; DOC-06 and DOC-09 say placed in service in 2025.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-16 p.2, 5: 'Federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return.' || DOC-06 p.1, 2: 'placed in service on July 15, 2025' || DOC-09 p.2, 14: 'Placed in service 7/15/2025'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: A federal rehabilitation credit cannot be claimed on a return for a year before the building is placed in service. The final cost certification and schedule govern over the memo.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Federal HTC and equity figures in the financial model are arithmetically inconsistent and conflict with the final cost certification and operating agreement.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 says QRE 24.6M, 20% rate, federal HTC 5.12M, and federal equity 4.5056M; DOC-06 says federal credit 4.92M; DOC-04 and DOC-11 say federal equity 4.3296M.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.2, 2.1-2.5: 'Qualified rehabilitation expenses: 24,600'; 'Federal historic tax credit rate: 20%'; 'Federal historic tax credit: $5,120,000'; 'Federal equity price per credit dollar: 0.82'; 'Federal investor equity: 4,505.6' || DOC-06 p.3, 4-5: 'Total qualified rehabilitation expenditures: 24,600,000'; 'Federal rehabilitation credit: 4,920,000' || DOC-04 p.1, Source 4: 'Federal historic tax credit equity $4,329,600' || DOC-11 p.13, 4.1(a): 'projected federal credits of $4,920,000 at 0.88 per credit dollar'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: 24.6M times 20% equals 4.92M, not 5.12M; 4.92M times 0.88 equals 4.3296M. The final cost certification and signed operating agreement govern over the model.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Misquote: DOC-05 2.4 reads 0.88, not 0.82. The conclusion is right, but one cited quote is not in the document.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Signed Virginia credit purchase agreement prices credits at $0.82, but the model, memo, email and draft use $0.85.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-12 says $0.82; DOC-13 draft and DOC-05, DOC-16 and DOC-15 use $0.85.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: The signed purchase agreement governs over the unsigned draft and later emails/memos unless an amendment is documented. The higher price overstates expected Virginia proceeds.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Budget shows a $600,000 funding gap, but the investor memo says the project is fully funded.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 total uses exceed total sources by $600,000; DOC-16 says all sources are committed and the project is fully funded.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-04 p.1, 12-25: 'Total sources $31,150,000'; 'Total uses $31,750,000'; 'Gap ($600,000)' || DOC-16 p.1, 2: 'The project is fully funded, with all sources committed and construction complete.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The budget and memo cannot both be true absent an additional source, and no additional source is documented. The budget is the detailed source and shows a gap.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Budget developer fee of $2.75M exceeds the operating agreement cap of $2.5M without documented investor consent.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 includes a $2,750,000 developer fee; DOC-11 caps the total development fee at $2,500,000 without prior written consent.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: No consent document is in the data room. The operating agreement is a signed legal document and governs the fee cap.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Operating agreement installment amounts sum to $4,429,600, not the stated $4,329,600; the 40% installment is misstated.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-11 states total capital contribution of $4,329,600; the four installment amounts add to $4,429,600.
Baseline Findings.Explanation: 40% of $4,329,600 is $1,731,840, not $1,831,840. The installment table overstates the total by $100,000.

Baseline Findings.Summary: The recapture guaranty cap is stated as $1.5M and $1.0M in the same operating agreement.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: The document contains two different legal caps for the same guaranty. The later or more specific provision would need clarification.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Developer plans to sell commercial unit C-1 during the compliance period, while the investor memo says no sale is planned and the operating agreement restricts transfers without consent.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-15 plans a sale of C-1 in June 2026; DOC-16 says no sale or transfer is planned during the credit period; DOC-11 prohibits sale of any unit during the compliance period without investor consent.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-15 p.12: 'We plan to sell commercial unit C-1 to Danville Arts Collective, targeting June 30, 2026.' || DOC-16 p.2, 7: 'No sale or transfer of any part of the property is planned during the credit period.' || DOC-11 p.24, 8.2: 'No sale or transfer of the Building or any unit during the Compliance Period without Investor Member consent'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: A sale during the five-year compliance period can create recapture risk and conflicts with the operating agreement absent investor consent. No consent is documented.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Equity bridge loan matures March 31, 2026, but its stated repayment source is installment 3 received June 30, 2026.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 says bridge matures 3/31/2026 and is repaid from federal equity installment 3; DOC-05 says installment 3 is received 6/30/2026.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: The repayment source arrives three months after maturity, creating a liquidity gap unless the bridge is extended, which is not documented.

Baseline Findings.Summary: GC agreement dated June 5, 2023 incorporates drawings dated July 20, 2023 and the Part 2 approval dated August 22, 2023.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-08 is entered June 5, 2023 but lists later drawings and the approved Part 2 application as contract documents; DOC-02 approval is dated August 22, 2023.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-08 p.1, 3-4: 'Contract Documents include the drawings and specifications issued by Hollins and Reade Architects dated July 20, 2023, and the approved Part 2 application.'; 'This Agreement is entered into as of June 5, 2023.' || DOC-02 p.1: 'August 22, 2023'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: A June 5 agreement cannot incorporate documents created or approved later without an amendment. The date conflict affects contract enforceability and approval sequencing.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Same candidate new case found by every run: contract dated before the documents it cites.

Baseline Findings.Summary: GC Notice to Proceed is dated June 5, 2023, but the construction schedule says construction started October 2, 2023.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-08 says contractor shall begin work on the NTP date of June 5, 2023; DOC-09 says construction start was 10/2/2023.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-08 p.1, 1: 'Notice to Proceed dated June 5, 2023.' || DOC-09 p.1, 3: 'Construction start 10/2/2023'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: If the NTP fixed the start date, the actual start was delayed by about four months; no change order or extension is documented.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Severity understated: expected High. Treats it as a delay and misses that a June start would come before Part 2 approval.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Project documents say 84 apartments, but the appraisal says 86 rental units.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-07 and DOC-03 say 84 apartments; DOC-10 says 86 units of rental housing.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-07 p.1, 1: 'converts the former Ashby Mill into 84 apartments' || DOC-03 p.1, 2: '84 apartments and 2 commercial suites' || DOC-10 p.2, 1: '86 units of rental housing'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The unit count mismatch affects appraisal, rent roll and underwriting assumptions. The architect and market study agree on 84; the appraisal is inconsistent.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Market study assumes absorption of 7 units per month, but the financial model assumes 12 units per month.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-03 projects 7 units per month; DOC-05 assumes 12 units per month.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-03 p.8, 4: 'We project an absorption pace of 7 units per month' || DOC-05 p.3, 3.2: 'Lease-up assumption: 12 units per month from the first unit delivered.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The two assumptions produce very different lease-up and stabilization timing. The market study is the demand source; the model assumption is inconsistent.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Model assumes Virginia credit proceeds on July 31, 2026, but the signed agreement requires closing within 30 days after DHR certification and has an April 30, 2026 outside date.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 assumes proceeds July 31, 2026; DOC-12 requires closing within 30 days after DHR certification and allows termination if certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: A July 31 closing is after the outside date and more than 30 days after a timely DHR certification. The timing conflict needs clarification.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Severity understated: expected High.

Baseline Findings.Summary: NPS Part 3 approval is supported only by an email; no NPS approval letter is in the data room.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-15 email says NPS approved Part 3 in October; DOC-09 says Part 3 was submitted 9/30/2025, but no approval document is included.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: Part 3 approval is critical to credit certification, and an email is not an approval letter. The data room lacks the authoritative NPS decision.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Budget labels parking lot and FF&E as qualified costs, while the final cost certification excludes parking and furniture.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-04 marks parking lot and FF&E as qualified costs; DOC-06 excludes parking and furniture from QRE.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-04 p.2, 31-34: 'Parking lot Yes $420,000'; 'Furniture, fixtures and equipment Yes $290,000' || DOC-06 p.3, 1: 'Costs for acquisition, land, site work outside the building, parking and furniture are excluded.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The $710,000 difference explains why budget qualified costs of $25.31M exceed final QRE of $24.6M. The final cost certification governs, so this is an estimate-stage classification issue.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Wrong class and severity: parking and furniture never qualify, so this is a Critical contradiction. Also calls the draft cost certification final.

Baseline Findings.Summary: Market study spells the county name as Pittsburgh in one place and Pittsylvania in another.

Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-03 p.2, 4: 'Pittsburgh County' || DOC-03 p.23, 65: 'Pittsylvania County'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: This is a typographical county-name inconsistency with no money or eligibility impact.

Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.2, 2.1-2.3: 'Qualified rehabilitation expenses: 24,600 ($ in thousands)2.2 Federal historic tax credit rate: 20%2.3 Federal historic tax credit: $5,120,000' || DOC-06 p.3, 4-5: 'Total qualified rehabilitation expenditures: 24,600,000 ... Federal rehabilitation credit: 4,920,000' || DOC-16 p.1, 4: 'The cost certification shows approximately $24.6 million of qualified rehabilitation expenses, generating $4.9M in federal credits.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: 20% x $24.6M = $4.92M, so $5.12M is arithmetically wrong and overstates the federal credit by $200,000; the CPA cost certification and investor memo align with $4.92M, so DOC-05 is unreliable.

Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-05 says federal equity price is 0.82 and federal investor equity is 4,505.6 ($000); DOC-11 says the Investor Member contributes $4,329,600 calculated on projected federal credits of $4,920,000 at 0.88 per credit dollar.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-05 p.2, 2.4-2.5: 'Federal equity price per credit dollar: 0.82.5 Federal investor equity: 4,505.6 ($ in thousands)' || DOC-11 p.13, 4.1 and 4.1(a): 'The Investor Member shall contribute a total of $4,329,600 to the capital of the Company ... The capital contribution has been calculated on projected federal credits of $4,920,000 at 0.88 per credit dollar.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: At $0.82 x $5.12M equity would be $4,198.4k; $4,505.6k is $0.88 x $5.12M; DOC-11 signed agreement's $4,329.6k is $0.88 x $4.92M, so DOC-05 mixes the price and credit amount.
Baseline Findings.Reviewer note: Knock-on of F01. Misreads DOC-05 2.4 as 0.82; it reads 0.88 (checked with two PDF text extractors). DeepSeek made the same misreading.

Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-12 signed says Buyer shall pay $0.82 per $1.00 of credit; DOC-05 says Virginia credit price is 0.85 and proceeds are 5,227.5 ($000); DOC-16 says Virginia credits sold at $0.85 per credit; DOC-13 unsigned draft says 0.85.
Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-12 p.3, 2.1: 'Buyer shall pay $0.82 per $1.00 of credit for all Credits transferred at Closing.' || DOC-05 p.2, 2.6-2.7: 'Virginia credit price per credit dollar: 0.85 ... Virginia credit proceeds: 5,227.5 ($ in thousands)' || DOC-16 p.1, 3: 'Virginia credits sold at $0.85 per credit.' || DOC-13 p.3, 2.1: 'Buyer shall pay $0.85 per $1.00 of credit for all Credits transferred at Closing.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The signed DOC-12 governs over the unsigned draft, model and memo; at $6.15M of credits, $0.82 yields $5.043M, not $5.2275M, and no signed amendment to $0.85 is in the data room.

Baseline Findings.Summary: DOC-15 says the building was placed in service on March 28 with the Phase 1 TCO, while DOC-06 and DOC-09 say July 15, 2025.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-15 says placed in service March 28 with Phase 1 TCO and work continues on floors 4 and 5; DOC-06 says placed in service July 15, 2025; DOC-09 lists placed in service 7/15/2025.

Work continues on floors 4 and 5.' || DOC-06 p.1, 2: 'The building was placed in service on July 15, 2025, being the date the completed rehabilitation was ready and available for its intended use.' || DOC-09 p.2, 14: 'Placed in service 7/15/2025'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: The placed-in-service date fixes the tax year and starts the compliance period; the date cannot be both March 28 and July 15, and the update itself indicates partial occupancy while upper floors remained incomplete.

Baseline Findings.Summary: DOC-16 says federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return, but DOC-06 and DOC-09 place the building in service in 2025.
Baseline Findings.Claims compared: DOC-16 says federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return; DOC-06 and DOC-09 say placed in service July 15, 2025.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: A credit for a building placed in service in 2025 cannot be claimed on the 2024 return; the investor memo conflicts with the cost certification and schedule.

Baseline Findings.Summary: DOC-06 names Riverside Heritage Development LLC as taxpayer, but DOC-01 and DOC-11 identify Ashby Mill Owner LLC as owner and credit claimant.

Baseline Findings.Explanation: The federal historic tax credit is claimed by the owner of the building; naming the developer as taxpayer is inconsistent and could affect who may claim the credit.

Baseline Findings.Summary: DOC-14 quotes vinyl standard-profile windows with simulated grilles, while DOC-02 and DOC-07 require wood windows replicating original profiles and muntin patterns.

Baseline Findings.Citations: DOC-14 p.1: 'Item 1 - Vinyl double-hung, standard profile412' and 'Units are white vinyl with a standard sash profile and simulated grilles between the glass.' || DOC-02 p.3, Condition 2: 'Replacement windows must replicate the original wood profiles in material, dimensions and muntin pattern.' || DOC-07 p.6, 1: 'Wood windows replicating original profiles, with true divided lites matching the historic muntin pattern and profile.'
Baseline Findings.Explanation: Vinyl standard-profile windows do not meet the approved Part 2 condition, and proceeding with them could jeopardize Part 3 certification.

Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-09 p.7: 'Federal credits delivered: 2025 7,290; 2026 to 2029 0' || DOC-08 p.9, II.C, 1: 'the credit for each Building is allowed ratably over the five taxable years beginning with the year in which that Building is placed in service'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Building A's credit runs 2025 to 2029 and Building B's from 2026. Front-loading the credit overstates the investor's early benefit and return.

Ground Truth.Summary: Virginia purchase agreement, signed after the review, still estimates $9.95M of credits
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-17 defines Estimated Credits as 25% of the expenses in Appendix 2, which still lists Building C and the parking deck and totals $39,800,000; 25% of the corrected $36,450,000 is $9,112,500 (DOC-09).
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-17 p.3, Section 1.4: 'twenty-five percent (25%) of the Eligible Rehabilitation Expenses set forth in Appendix 2, which the parties acknowledge to be ... ($9,950,000)' || DOC-17 p.26, Appendix 2: 'Building C $2,750,000', 'Site and parking $600,000', 'Total $39,800,000' || DOC-09 p.3: 'Virginia credit 9,112.5' || DOC-23 p.1, 3: 'Virginia HTC: $9.95M'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The agreement was signed in September 2024, after the QRE was corrected, yet it uses the pre-review figure. The buyer is expecting $837,500 more credits than the project will generate.

Ground Truth.Summary: Deck and snapshot quote $0.84 for Virginia credits; the signed price is $0.80
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-05 slide 13 and DOC-23 say $0.84; DOC-17 Section 2.1 says $0.80.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-05 slide 13: 'Virginia HTC sold at $0.84 per credit' || DOC-23 p.1, 3: '$9.95M at $0.84' || DOC-17 p.5, Section 2.1: 'Buyer shall pay eighty cents ($0.80), without adjustment for any change in market conditions'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The snapshot was sent to the same buyer who signed at $0.80. The signed agreement governs.

Ground Truth.Summary: Deck and snapshot say Part 2 was approved without conditions; it was conditional
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-05 slide 14 and DOC-23 say no conditions; DOC-02 is a conditional approval with two conditions.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-05 slide 14: 'NPS Part 2 approved August 2023 - no conditions' || DOC-23 p.1, 5: 'NPS Part 2 approved without conditions' || DOC-02 p.1: 'NPS - APPROVED WITH CONDITIONS ... Conditions: page 4'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The conditions drive the unit count and the cornice risk. Hiding them misleads the reader about certification risk.

Ground Truth.Summary: Management agreement is signed by the owner, although the master lease makes the master tenant the operator
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-22 has the Owner engage the Manager; DOC-12 Section 2.2 makes the Lessee responsible for leasing and management.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-22 p.1: 'Owner hereby engages Manager as the exclusive agent of Owner to operate, lease and manage the Property' || DOC-12 p.4, Section 2.2: 'Lessee ... shall be solely responsible for leasing, management and day-to-day operation, including the engagement of any property manager'
Ground Truth.Explanation: In a lease pass-through the master tenant must actually operate the property for the lease to be respected. A management contract with the owner undercuts that.
Ground Truth.Alternative readings: The owner may have signed as agent for the master tenant under a provision not in the excerpt.
Ground Truth.Open questions: Is there an assignment of the PMA to the master tenant?

Ground Truth.Summary: Revised deck says the investor joins the owner entity; the signed agreement puts it in the master tenant
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-05 slide 8 says the investor is admitted to Calder Works Owner LLC; DOC-11 admits it to Calder Works Master Tenant LLC.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-05 slide 8: 'Federal HTC investor admitted to Calder Works Owner LLC' || DOC-11 p.1: 'Operating Agreement of Calder Works Master Tenant LLC ... as Investor Member'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The structure changed to a master lease after the investor review. The deck describes the old structure.

Ground Truth.Summary: Loan amendment signature block misnames the borrower
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-13 p.39 signs as 'Calder Work Owners LLC'; the borrower is Calder Works Owner LLC.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-13 p.39: 'BORROWER: Calder Work Owners LLC, by its manager' || DOC-13 p.1: 'Calder Works Owner LLC, Borrower'
Ground Truth.Explanation: A misnamed signatory is a clean-up item for counsel, not a money issue.

Ground Truth.Summary: Revised deck shows total development cost of $49.8M; the revised budget says $48.6M
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-05 slide 15: 'Total development cost $49,800,000' || DOC-10 p.1, line 14: 'Total development cost $48,600,000'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The $1.2M gap is exactly the developer fee cut. The deck's sources and uses was not rebuilt.

Ground Truth.Summary: Part 3 for Building A was only filed, yet the installment it triggers has been requested
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-19 says Part 3 was filed October 20, 2025 and installment 2 was requested pending Part 3; DOC-11 Section 3.2(b) pays on receipt of Part 3 approval.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-19 p.22: 'Part 3 request for A submitted to SHPO on October 20' || DOC-19 p.24: 'Investor installment 2 drawdown notice issued, subject to Part 3' || DOC-11 p.15, Section 3.2(b): 'upon receipt by the Investor Member of a copy of the National Park Service's approval of the Part 3 request for Building A'
Ground Truth.Explanation: No Part 3 approval is in the data room, and given the cornice removal it may not be granted. The $2,507,760 installment is not yet due.

Ground Truth.Summary: No Section 50(d) election statement for Building A is in the data room
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-12 requires the lessor to deliver the election statement within 30 days after each building's placed-in-service date; Building A was placed in service September 30, 2025.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-12 p.29, Section 18.3: 'shall deliver a copy of the election statement, as filed, to Lessee and the Investor Member within thirty (30) days after the placed-in-service date of each Building' || DOC-19 p.22: 'Building A: certificate of occupancy issued September 30; placed in service'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The statement was due by October 30, 2025. Without it, the credit cannot be confirmed as passing to the master tenant and its investor.

Ground Truth.Summary: Market study counts about 134 units, before NPS reduced the count
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-03 (March 2023) plans about 134 units, subject to historic review; the final count is 128 (DOC-22).
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-03 p.1, 2: 'approximately 134 dwelling units distributed across all three structures ... preliminary and may change upon completion of historic review and final design' || DOC-22 p.3, Section 1.2: 'one hundred twenty-eight (128) dwelling units'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The study predates the Part 2 condition and says its count may change. No later document relies on it.

Ground Truth.Summary: Appraisal counts 134 units from preliminary plans
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-21 (June 2023) uses 134 units per the sponsor's preliminary plans; final count is 128.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-21 p.2, 1: 'preliminary plans dated February 2023, which contemplate 134 units of rental housing ... historic review was then pending' || DOC-22 p.3, Section 1.2: 'one hundred twenty-eight (128) dwelling units'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The appraisal predates the August 2023 Part 2 decision and states its basis.

Ground Truth.Summary: Superseded deck v3 shows the pre-review QRE and a Section 6418 sale
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-04 (February 2024) shows $39.8M QRE and a Section 6418 transfer at $0.91; it predates the investor review.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-04 slide 6: 'Qualified rehabilitation expenditures: $39.8M' || DOC-04 slide 9: 'monetized via IRC Section 6418 transfer at $0.91'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Deck v3 is the version the investor reviewed and was replaced by v4. Its errors are the subject of the review. Flag the errors in v4 and the snapshot, not in v3.
Ground Truth.Alternative readings: A reviewer may still note that v3 remains in the data room without a superseded marking.

Ground Truth.Summary: Appraisal area and management agreement area differ because they measure different things
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-21 gives 214,600 SF gross for all buildings; DOC-22 gives 168,300 net rentable SF for Buildings A and B.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-21 p.2, 2: 'Gross building area, all three structures ...: 214,600 square feet' || DOC-22 p.3, Section 1.3: 'approximately 168,300 net rentable square feet'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Gross area of three buildings and net rentable area of two are different measures. Both can be right.

Ground Truth.Summary: Budget total includes Building C and the parking deck while QRE excludes them
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-10 total development cost of $48.6M includes $3.35M of Building C and parking costs; the QRE schedule excludes them.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-10 p.1, lines 9-10: 'Building C shell (non-QRE) $2,750,000; Parking deck (non-QRE) $600,000' || DOC-10 p.2, line 5: '$36,450,000'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Total cost and qualified cost are different measures. The budget labels the excluded lines clearly.

Ground Truth.Summary: GC price of $36.5M sits close to QRE of $36.45M, but they cover different scopes
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-14 GMP is $36,500,000 including Building C and the parking deck; QRE is $36,450,000 including qualified soft costs.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-14 p.1, 2: 'guaranteed not to exceed Thirty-Six Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($36,500,000), which sum is allocated ... among the rehabilitation of Buildings A and B, shell work on Building C and construction of the parking deck' || DOC-10 p.2, line 5: '$36,450,000'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The near match is a coincidence of two different measures, not a rounding of one figure.

Ground Truth.Summary: Tax memo's QRE estimate matches the budget after rounding
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-08 estimates about $36.5 million; DOC-10 says $36,450,000.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-08 p.13, II.E, 1: 'qualified rehabilitation expenditures for Buildings A and B will total approximately $36.5 million' || DOC-10 p.2, line 5: '$36,450,000'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Rounding only.

Ground Truth.Summary: Model credits tab QRE matches the budget
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-09 p.3: 'Qualified rehabilitation expenditures 36,450' || DOC-10 p.2, line 5: '$36,450,000'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Same figure in thousands.

Ground Truth.Summary: Master tenant name written two ways
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-12 signs as 'Calder Works Master Tenant, L.L.C.'; DOC-11 uses 'Calder Works Master Tenant LLC'.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-12 p.38: 'LESSEE: Calder Works Master Tenant, L.L.C.' || DOC-11 p.1: 'Calder Works Master Tenant LLC'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Same entity.

Ground Truth.Summary: Notice to proceed date written in two formats
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-14 says September 5, 2023; DOC-16 says 9/5/2023.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-14 p.1, 1: 'notice was issued on September 5, 2023' || DOC-16 p.2, 3: 'commencing with the start of physical work on 9/5/2023'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Same date.

Ground Truth.Summary: Building A placed-in-service date agrees between the cost certification and the update
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-16 and DOC-19 both give September 30, 2025.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-16 p.2, 2: 'Building A was placed in service on September 30, 2025, the date on which its certificate of occupancy was issued' || DOC-19 p.22: 'Building A: certificate of occupancy issued September 30; placed in service'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Consistent.

Ground Truth.Summary: Credit rates agree between the model and the cost certification
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-09 and DOC-16 both apply 20% federal and 25% Virginia.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-09 p.3: 'Federal credit rate 20%' and 'Virginia credit rate 25%' || DOC-16 p.3, 2: 'Credit rates applied: twenty percent (20%) federal; twenty-five percent (25%) Virginia'
Ground Truth.Explanation: Consistent.

Ground Truth.Summary: Investor installments add up to the stated contribution
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-11 Section 3.2 installments of $1,253,880, $2,507,760, $1,880,820 and $626,940 total $6,269,400, matching Section 3.1(a).
Ground Truth.Explanation: The installments are correct. Unlike HTC01, this schedule has no error, so a model that flags it is pattern-matching.

Ground Truth.Summary: The stale Exhibit B would trigger a $576,200 downward adjuster even though the price already reflects the corrected credits
Ground Truth.Claims compared: Section 3.4(a) measures any shortfall against Projected Federal Credits, which Exhibit B sets at $7,960,000; the credits on the corrected base are $7,290,000 (DOC-16, DOC-09).
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-11 p.18, Section 3.4(a): 'If the Federal Credits finally determined ... are less than the Projected Federal Credits, the Managing Member shall pay ... the product of the amount of such shortfall and the Federal Credit Price' || DOC-11 p.66, Exhibit B: 'Projected Federal Credits: twenty percent (20%) of Projected QRE, or $7,960,000' || DOC-16 p.3, 1: '$36,450,000, of which $18,900,000 is attributable to Building A and $17,550,000 to Building B' || DOC-09 p.3: 'Federal credit 7,290'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The shortfall of $670,000 times $0.86 gives a $576,200 adjuster owed by the Managing Member, although the $6,269,400 contribution was already priced on $7,290,000. The same agreement prices the deal on one credit figure and measures the adjuster against another.
Ground Truth.Alternative readings: The acknowledged $6,269,400 in Section 3.1(a) may be read as evidence that the parties intended $7,290,000.
Ground Truth.Open questions: Will the parties amend Exhibit B before the cost certification is final?

Ground Truth.Summary: Building B's delay triggers a two-cent price step-down that no document reflects
Ground Truth.Claims compared: Section 3.4(c) cuts the federal price by $0.02 if either building is not placed in service by December 31, 2025; Building B is expected March 31, 2026; the budget still carries $6,269,400 at $0.86.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-11 p.18, Section 3.4(c): 'If either Building has not been placed in service on or before December 31, 2025, the Federal Credit Price shall be reduced ... by two cents ($0.02)' || DOC-06 p.3, Comment 4: 'conditioned on both Buildings being placed in service by December 31, 2025, failing which the price will step down' || DOC-16 p.4, 1: 'on or about March 31, 2026' || DOC-19 p.24: 'now forecasting CO on or about March 31, 2026' || DOC-10 p.1, line 2: 'Federal HTC equity (master tenant) $6,269,400'
Ground Truth.Explanation: At $0.84 the contribution becomes $7,290,000 x 0.84 = $6,123,600, a reduction of $145,800 taken from installments not yet paid. Neither the budget nor the December update recognizes it.

Ground Truth.Summary: The Virginia buyer can walk away unless both buildings are finally certified by June 30, 2026, which the schedule makes unlikely
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-17 Section 5.2 requires Final Certification for each Building by June 30, 2026; Building B is not expected to be placed in service until March 31, 2026, and Building A's Part 3 was only submitted in October 2025.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-17 p.12, Section 5.2: 'If Final Certification has not been obtained for each of the Buildings on or before June 30, 2026 (the Outside Date), Buyer may terminate this Agreement' || DOC-16 p.4, 1: 'on or about March 31, 2026' || DOC-19 p.22: 'Part 3 request for A submitted to SHPO on October 20'
Ground Truth.Explanation: State final certification follows completion and federal Part 3 review. Three months from Building B's certificate of occupancy is tight, and Building A's Part 3 is exposed to the cornice removal. Nothing in the data room extends the Outside Date.
Ground Truth.Alternative readings: Certification could arrive in time if reviews are fast.
Ground Truth.Open questions: Has the buyer agreed to extend the Outside Date?

Ground Truth.Summary: The management fee is above the cap in the operating agreement
Ground Truth.Claims compared: DOC-11 Section 7.2 caps any management fee at 3.5% of Gross Operating Revenues; DOC-22 Section 4.1 pays 4% of Gross Collections.
Ground Truth.Citations: DOC-11 p.34, Section 7.2: 'No management agreement shall provide for a management fee exceeding three and one-half percent (3.5%) of Gross Operating Revenues' || DOC-22 p.9, Section 4.1: 'a monthly management fee equal to four percent (4%) of Gross Collections'
Ground Truth.Explanation: The fee breaches the cap by half a percentage point of revenue, and the agreement was not approved under Section 7.2. It is also signed by the owner rather than the master tenant (see HTC02-020).
